title: Literally check #4601's radical-invariance cost formula on a noncommutative local algebra (F4[e;Frob]/e^2) and three further local rings: holds on every target (no new κ)
body:
Independent literal check of petalas's #4601 (head `4b2322fc`), radical invariance of right-vector costs. It covers a **noncommutative** local algebra, which #4601 proves but does not enumerate. **It agrees.** No new κ.

## Method

`research/pr4601-noncommutative-check/verify.py` uses the standard library only and runs in about 4 s.

- **Literal costs.** Costs come from closing products of paid factors I + u yᵀ and free GL₂(K) maps.
- **No shortcuts from #4601.** There is no pivot test and nothing is imported.
- **Coset reduction** uses g P(u,y) g⁻¹ = P(gu, g⁻ᵀy).

## Rings and results

Every invertible target was checked:

- **F₄[e; Frobenius]/e² over F₂ (noncommutative; ω·e ≠ e·ω):** 46,080 targets;
- F₂[x]/x³: 1,536 targets;
- F₃[e]/e²: 3,888 targets;
- F₂[e]/e² control: 96 targets.

On all four rings:

- **#4601's formula holds.** cost_R(M) = max(δ_R(M), cost_D(M̄)), and two-factor invariance holds on every target.
- **The control matches.** It reproduces #4601's published k = 1 histogram [6, 54, 36, 0].
- **Failure control.** The residue cost alone is wrong on 23,130, 1,530, 3,840 and 90 targets respectively.

## Limitation

With one component no target reaches cost 3, so the noncommutative three-factor regime (k ≥ q+1) is not covered here.
